question: Does windowed-photometry polish DISCRIMINATE truth, or does it also drive far/phantom seed-pairs to Band A?
hypothesis: Pairs far from truth (or off the truth attractor) stay Band D under the same window-as-objective polish; no phantom Band A appears, so the window objective is a genuine discriminator and not just a truth-seeded fit.

predictions.case: seed 119, oracle-FAR pair (endpoints >90° off the truth pair)
seed 119, second-nearest attractor pair (one of the 7 attractors, not the truth one)
predictions.expected_outcome: uncertain — could phantom into Band A; this is the crux

predictions.case: seed 116 (a different tumbler) with its own oracle-nearest pair
predictions.expected_outcome: reproduces Band A (replication of the s106 mechanism on a 2nd seed)

confirm_criteria: 0 phantom Band A across >=5 non-truth pairs on seed 119, AND the s106 mechanism reproduces Band A on >=1 second seed.
refute_criteria: >=1 oracle-far pair reaches Band A (the window objective is not discriminating), OR the mechanism fails to reproduce on any second seed.
required_artefacts: rho-band table over all tested pairs (truth-near, second-attractor, far)
window-objective overlay plot (ρ vs window choice per pair)

analytical_probe.cheap_path: re-score the cached s106 polished checkpoints for the far/second-attractor pairs against truth hi-fi LC (no new optimisation), instead of running 8 fresh windowed polishes
analytical_probe.why_insufficient: discrimination requires running the window-as-objective LM polish ON the far pairs to see whether they phantom into Band A; the cached checkpoints only hold the truth-near pair, so the far-pair endpoint is not in any existing result.json — there is nothing to re-score.
